findings.current: And, in contrast, a being born blessed by every living thing in the world: a Dragon.
findings.defect: “Every living thing” narrows 만물, which includes all things in the world.
findings.rationale: The source contrasts the cursed undead with a Dragon blessed by the whole of creation, not only living creatures.
findings.replacement: And, in contrast, a being born with the blessing of all creation: a Dragon.
findings.source: 그와는 반대로 온 세상 만물의 축복 속에서 탄생한 존재, 드래곤(Dragon).

findings.current: Now I understand how you, a mere undead—no, a mere Skeleton—came to possess such power.
findings.defect: “No” makes Morgoth correct himself; the source compounds the insult.
findings.rationale: 그것도 adds the more specific, contemptuous description without retracting “undead.”
findings.replacement: Now I understand how you, a mere undead—a Skeleton, at that—came to possess such power.
findings.source: 한낮 언데드, 그것도 스켈레톤에 불과한 자네가 어떻게 그 정도의 힘을 지니게 되었는지 이제야 이해가 되는군.

findings.defect: The singular “you” loses Morgoth’s shift to addressing the Skeleton King and others together.
findings.rationale: 너희 is plural; Morgoth’s conclusion extends beyond the opponent standing before him.
findings.replacement: I don’t underestimate any of you.

summary: Three actionable fidelity findings: the scope of the Dragon’s blessing, Morgoth’s compounded insult, and his plural address.
